title: Ranveer Singh brings home a Rs. 1.95 crore electric luxury sedan; all you need to know about his BMW i7
raw_summary:
Bollywood star Ranveer Singh has added a new luxury car to his garage, with the actor taking delivery of the BMW i7 50 xDrive, the all-electric version of the German automaker’s flagship 7 Series sedan. The luxury electric car is priced at Rs. 1.95 crore (ex-showroom), making it a significant addition to the actor’s already impressive collection of automobiles.

The acquisition comes shortly after Ranveer was unveiled as BMW India’s brand ambassador and introduced the company’s latest 7 Series range at a launch event in New Delhi in September. The actor’s association with the brand now gets an interesting personal touch, with the star bringing home one of its flagship electric offerings.

The BMW i7 50 xDrive M Sport combines the presence and comfort expected from a flagship luxury sedan with the benefits of an all-electric powertrain. The model produces 455 hp and 600 Nm of torque, with a claimed 0-100 kmph acceleration time of 5.5 seconds. It features a 112.5 kWh battery pack and offers a claimed driving range of up to 728 km on the WLTP cycle.

The car also places considerable emphasis on passenger comfort and in-cabin technology. Its features include a large rear-seat entertainment screen, a premium Bowers & Wilkins sound system, executive lounge seating and an upgraded infotainment setup. The new i7 is locally manufactured at BMW Group’s Chennai facility, making India the only country outside Germany to produce the electric flagship.

For Ranveer, whose larger-than-life personality often extends to his automobile choices, the i7 represents a move towards electric luxury without compromising on performance or road presence. With its imposing design, technology-led cabin and all-electric credentials, the BMW is a fitting addition to the actor’s collection.

title: Ronit Roy leases Andheri west office space for Rs 1.39 crores over five years
raw_summary:
Actor Ronit Roy has leased a commercial office space in Mumbai’s Andheri West for a total rent of approximately Rs 1.39 crores over a five-year period. The transaction adds to the actor’s reported real estate holdings in the city, where he also owns a residential apartment in Versova.

According to a Business Standard report citing property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix, the office measures 950 square feet and is situated on the fourth floor of Vastu Prestige, near City Mall in Andheri West.

The leave-and-licence agreement was registered on June 12, with the lease commencing on July 10. The agreement will remain valid until July 9, 2031, covering a total tenure of 60 months.

As per the report, the commercial premises have been leased to Kerawi Care (OPC) Private Limited, represented by its director, Vandana Verma. Roy is listed as the licensor in the agreement, while the company is the licensee.

The office space carries a monthly rent of Rs 2.1 lakhs, while the security deposit has been set at Rs 6.5 lakhs. The total rent payable over the five-year period amounts to Rs 1,39,24,584. The agreement also provides for an annual rent escalation of 5%, along with a lock-in period of 36 months for both parties.

The terms further specify the division of property-related expenses between the parties. Roy, as the licensor, will be responsible for property taxes, maintenance charges and non-occupancy charges. Meanwhile, the tenant will pay electricity bills according to actual consumption. The report also noted that the agreement does not mention any designated car parking space for the office.

This is not the actor’s first reported real estate transaction in Mumbai. According to a Hindustan Times report citing property registration documents accessed by IndexTap.com, Roy purchased a 4,258-square-foot apartment in the Lodha Versova project in 2024 for Rs 18.94 crores. The property reportedly came with four car parking spaces.

A separate Economic Times report published in September 2026 stated that Roy and his family reside in Versova, where they expanded their home over the years by acquiring adjoining apartments.

Apart from his acting career, Roy is known for his roles as Mihir Virani in Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi and Rishabh Bajaj in Kasautii Zindagii Kay. He also owns Ace Security and Protection, a security agency that has reportedly served several prominent Bollywood personalities, including Amitabh Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan and Aamir Khan. The agency also provided protection to Saif Ali Khan following the attack on the actor.

title: Nana Patekar death: Goa Police register “unnatural death” case, to begin further enquiry
raw_summary:
Veteran actor Nana Patekar was cremated with full state honours at his Donje farmhouse in Pune on Thursday night, October 8, following his death at the age of 75. Meanwhile, Panaji Police have registered an unnatural death case under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and further enquiry into the circumstances surrounding his death is underway.

According to police records, Nana Patekar was brought dead to the casualty ward of Manipal Hospital in Bambolim from his residence at Ocean Park, Dona Paula, Goa. The enquiry is being led by PSI Nitin Naik.

The registration of an unnatural death case is part of the police procedure to examine the circumstances surrounding a death. The case registration, by itself, does not establish any wrongdoing. Further details are awaited as the enquiry progresses.

title: Meezaan Jafri headlines Killer Jeans' Genes of India campaign
raw_summary:
Killer Jeans, one of India’s first homegrown denim brands, is changing the conversation around denim fashion in the country through its Genes of India campaign, with actor Meezaan Jafri as the face of the brand. The campaign looks at how denim has become a part of everyday dressing across India, and how each region, city and generation styles it in its own way.

Denim is now one of the most versatile and widely worn categories in Indian fashion. It is part of wardrobes across age groups and occasions, and it continues to influence how younger consumers dress for work, travel, social settings and celebrations. Genes of India builds on this shift, presenting denim as a shared part of Indian style, from Kashmir to Kanyakumari.

Meezaan Jafri, as brand ambassador, connects with an audience that sees denim as a core part of personal style and not as a casual alternative. His styling reflects the fits and combinations that younger consumers are choosing today. “Denim is something almost everyone in India relates to, whatever their background or city,” said Meezaan Jafri. “What I like about Genes of India is that it doesn’t ask people to dress a certain way. It recognises that everyone wears denim differently, and that is what makes it ours.”

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Killer Jeans (@killerjeansofficial)

The latest addition to the Killer line-up, Neo Flare brings a contemporary perspective to the classic flare silhouette. Designed to sit slim through the hip, thigh and knee, the fit gradually opens below the knee to create a longer, leaner profile. Neo Flare brings a fresh dimension to everyday denim and pairs effortlessly with everything from sneakers to boots.

The collection is complemented by Selvedge Denim, known for its distinctive character, texture and craftsmanship, alongside Killer’s range of fabric innovations. K-Tech Denim offers a lighter feel, SoftPro Denim delivers a softer hand-feel, while Cool Core Denim is designed to provide comfort across changing weather conditions. Together, these innovations reflect Killer’s focus on combining contemporary denim design with fit, functionality and comfort.

“Denim has always been something I’ve felt people can make their own. In India, that feels even more interesting because the way you wear it changes from city to city, from generation to generation, and from person to person. That’s what drew me to Genes of India; it’s not about one definition of denim, but about all the different ways we style it, live in it and make it part of who we are” said Hemant Jain, Joint Managing Director, Kewal Kiran Clothing Limited.

Killer’s contribution to the category begins with its products. The brand designs for Indian consumers, with attention to fit, comfort and finish, and places weight on Indian manufacturing and the craftsmanship that goes into making denim. Through Genes of India, it aims to bring that work into focus and to support a stronger domestic denim category, where consumers can find quality, trend-relevant options made in India.

Killer believes Indian denim has significant room to grow, driven by rising fashion awareness, a greater willingness to experiment and demand for quality, locally made products.

title: Hanuman Ansh, Cocktail 2 create tourism BOOM: Kainchi Dham witnesses MASSIVE crowds; Italy bookings jump 38%
raw_summary:
Films have often influenced the travel plans of moviegoers, inspiring them to visit destinations they have admired on the big screen. Switzerland became a dream destination for many Indians after its picturesque locations were showcased in Yash Chopra's films. Kaho Naa Pyaar Hai (2000) encouraged viewers to explore New Zealand, while Spain found a place on travellers' wish lists after Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011). Similarly, 3 Idiots (2009) made Ladakh's Pangong Lake a must-visit destination. In recent times, two films have once again demonstrated the power of cinema in boosting tourism – Hanuman Ansh and Cocktail 2.

Last weekend, videos and pictures emerged of tourists and devotees thronging Kainchi Dham near Nainital, Uttarakhand. The surge in footfalls has been partly attributed to the sleeper blockbuster Hanuman Ansh, which is based on the life of Neeb Karori Baba, whose ashram is situated at Kainchi Dham.

A recent report in Bombay Times, published before the October 2 weekend rush, quoted Sanjeev Kumar, General Manager, Naukuchia House, Naukuchiatal – IHCL SeleQtions, as saying, “The interest around Hanuman Ansh, Neem Karoli Baba and Kainchi Dham has renewed attention on the spiritual landscape of Kumaon. Film-led interest can encourage travellers to look beyond the screen and discover the local culture, faith, food, people and landscape. That is when storytelling becomes meaningful for a destination – when a film sparks curiosity and leads to a more personal journey.”

However, the sudden popularity has also brought its share of problems. ThePrint published a detailed report on how locals are struggling to cope with the influx of tourists in the post-Hanuman Ansh era. The report revealed that rooms which normally cost Rs. 2,000-3,000 per night were being offered for as much as Rs. 7,000 during the recent rush. The massive crowds also led to traffic congestion and put pressure on local infrastructure.

This is also an example of the flip side of film tourism, where a destination becomes so popular that it struggles to accommodate the influx of visitors. The situation has prompted authorities to consider stricter measures. According to reports, the administration is planning to introduce a registration system for visitors, initially on weekends, to regulate the crowds and ensure a smoother experience for devotees.

On the other hand, Italy has once again caught the imagination of Indian moviegoers, and the credit partly goes to Cocktail 2, starring Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon and Rashmika Mandanna. A significant portion of the film's first half is set in picturesque Italian locations such as Catania, Noto, Siracusa, Castellammare del Golfo, Avola and Milan. These places have been beautifully captured on the big screen, giving viewers yet another reason to consider Italy for their next holiday.

According to the Bombay Times report, Aloke Bajpai, Group CEO, ixigo, revealed, “Since Cocktail 2 was released, bookings on our site to and from Italy are up 38% YoY.”

He further stated, “According to Great Indian Travel Index report, released last year, YoY bookings on ixigo to cities across the Northeast grew sharply, Dimapur +77%, Agartala +48%, and Guwahati and Imphal +44% each, with shows like The Family Man helping bring these destinations into the spotlight. We are seeing the same internationally. Sicily, featured in The White Lotus, The Odyssey and Cocktail 2, is a great example.”

The developments once again underline the influence of cinema beyond the box office. While films can introduce audiences to destinations they may never have considered visiting, the growing popularity of these places also raises questions about whether local infrastructure is equipped to handle the sudden influx. Hanuman Ansh and Cocktail 2 are two contrasting examples of this phenomenon, showing how the magic of the movies can translate into real-world travel, economic opportunities and, at times, unexpected challenges.

title: Awarapan 2 gets OTT premiere: Emraan Hashmi starrer starts streaming on Prime Video
raw_summary:
On October 9, 2026, Prime Video announced the exclusive global streaming premiere of Vishesh Bhatt’s Awarapan 2, the Hindi action drama that brought back Emraan Hashmi as one of his most-remembered characters. The return of Shivam comes nearly two decades after Awarapan, directed by Mohit Suri, became a defining film for a generation of viewers, with its brooding protagonist, poignant storytelling, and soulful music leaving a lasting imprint on popular culture.

Directed by Nitin Kakkar, Awarapan 2 builds on that familiarity, while taking Shivam into a next chapter, blending the emotional intensity of his story with high-octane action and the nostalgic musical sensibility audiences remember from the era. The film also stars Disha Patani, Shabana Azmi, Puran Gabbi, Vijayant Kohli, and Suvinder Vicky in pivotal roles, and weaves romance, action, and drama against the backdrop of the criminal underworld.

Vishesh Bhatt brings Awarapan 2, the second chapter of the blockbuster franchise. In a remote Rajasthan village, Shivam Pandit grieves at his beloved’s grave, questioning his purpose, his life. Having withdrawn from the world of crime and carrying the guilt of a past he cannot alter, he has resigned himself to a life in solitude. Then, an unexpected bond gives him a glimpse of something he had long thought beyond his reach - a reason to care, to hope, and perhaps to live differently.

But fate has other plans. Drawn into Bangkok’s cartel war, Shivam is forced back into the darkness he had left behind. Amid violence, betrayal and an unexpected chance in love, he finds himself responsible for something beyond himself. As the lives of those he has come to care for become entwined with his own, Shivam must confront the choices that brought him here - and decide what he is willing to fight for.

title: Nana Patekar cremated at Pune farmhouse with Full State Honours; son Malhar Patekar performs last rites
raw_summary:
Veteran actor Nana Patekar was cremated at his Pune farmhouse on Thursday, October 8, following his sudden demise earlier that morning. The actor was accorded full state honours, as announced by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, in recognition of his contribution to Indian cinema and his social welfare initiatives. Fadnavis, along with Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, was also seen paying his respects to the late actor at Pune airport.

Although Nana Patekar passed away in Goa, his mortal remains were brought to Pune in accordance with his wishes. According to reports, the actor had expressed his desire to be cremated at his Donje farmhouse in Pune. His son, Malhar Patekar, performed the last rites and lit the funeral pyre in the presence of family members, friends and colleagues from the film industry.

Several prominent personalities attended the funeral to pay their final respects to the veteran actor. Among those present were Jackie Shroff, producer Sajid Nadiadwala and filmmaker Anil Sharma, along with other members of the entertainment fraternity. The gathering reflected the impact Patekar had made through his work over a career spanning several decades.

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Bollywood Hungama🎥 (@realbollywoodhungama)

The Maharashtra government's decision to accord him a state funeral recognised not only his cinematic legacy but also his contributions to society through the Naam Foundation, which he co-founded with actor Makarand Anaspure to support drought-affected farmers and rural communities.

Nana Patekar's demise: What happened?

Nana Patekar, a Padma Shri recipient known for his acclaimed performances across Hindi and Marathi cinema, passed away at the age of 75 in the early hours of Thursday, October 8, 2026.

According to reports, the actor suffered a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. He was found unresponsive early in the morning and rushed to Manipal Hospital, where medical personnel reportedly attempted cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for approximately 45 minutes. However, he could not be revived and was declared dead at around 5:20 AM IST. His son, Malhar Patekar, subsequently confirmed the news.

Known for his intense screen presence and memorable performances, Patekar leaves behind a significant body of work spanning multiple genres and languages. His passing has prompted tributes from colleagues, admirers and members of the film fraternity, as the industry remembers an actor whose contributions extended beyond the screen.

title: Gauahar Khan sells Versova duplex for Rs 6.01 crores, bought it for Rs 3.2 crores in 2014
raw_summary:
Gauahar Khan has sold her duplex apartment in Mumbai’s Versova for Rs 6.01 crores, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix. Khan had purchased the property in November 2014 for Rs 3.2 crores, indicating an appreciation of around 88% over nearly 12 years.

The property transaction was registered on September 24, 2026. The apartment is located in Versova Shiv Kutir Co-operative Housing Society Ltd., situated in S.V.P. Nagar, Versova, Andheri West. The duplex occupies two floors of the building and is positioned on a higher floor.

As per the registration documents, the property has a super built-up area of 2,340 sq ft (217.47 sq m), while its built-up area measures 1,872 sq ft (173.98 sq m). The documents do not mention any car parking being included in the transaction.

The duplex was sold for a consideration value of Rs 6.01 crores, with the purchasers paying Rs 36.06 lakhs as stamp duty. Khan had acquired the apartment for Rs 3.2 crores in November 2014. This means the recorded consideration value increased by Rs 2.81 crores during the period, translating into an appreciation of nearly 88% on the original purchase price.

Based on the latest consideration value and the built-up area of 1,872 sq ft, the transaction works out to approximately Rs 32,100 per sq ft. Calculated against the super built-up area of 2,340 sq ft, the rate comes to around Rs 25,700 per sq ft. These figures are based on the consideration value mentioned in the registration document.

title: Prasanna Bisht starrer Bokshi release postponed to December 4 after CBFC review over witchcraft and gruesome violence
raw_summary:
The theatrical release of Prasanna Bisht-starrer Bokshi has been postponed from October 9 to December 4, 2026, following its recent certification process with the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). The film was referred by the CBFC’s Examining Committee to the Revising Committee for further review over its supernatural themes, depiction of witchcraft, gruesome violence and bloodshed.

Directed by Bhargav Saikia and written by debutant screenwriter and executive producer Harsh Vaibhav, Bokshi has now been cleared by the Revising Committee with an ‘A’ certificate and minimal modifications. The makers have decided to push the release to December to accommodate the certification-related delay and allow more time for a full-scale theatrical campaign.

Lorien Motion Pictures announced the revised release date on October 8, confirming that the folk-horror film will now arrive in select cinemas across India on December 4. The production house shared an official statement explaining the decision. The statement read, "Due to its supernatural themes, depiction of witchcraft, and gruesome violence, BOKSHI was recently referred by the CBFC's Examining Committee to the Revising Committee for further review. We are thrilled to share that the Revising Committee has now cleared the film with an "A" certificate with minimal modifications.

It further said, “To ensure a seamless theatrical rollout, we have made the difficult decision to postpone the release of BOKSHI in India, originally set for 9 October 2026. We are working hard behind the scenes to bring you the film in the best possible manner. We deeply appreciate our partners, media, content creators, and, above all, our audience for your patience and unwavering support. This is just a brief pause. BOKSHI will now release in select cinemas on 4 December 2026!"

The film’s trailer, released a few weeks ago, has reportedly received an encouraging response, particularly among younger audiences and fans of horror and genre cinema. Bokshi blends folk-horror, coming-of-age elements and mystery, with its story following Anahita, a troubled teenager whose school trek to a remote prehistoric site leads her towards an ancient legend.

The film stars Prasanna Bisht, Mansi Multani and Siddharth Shaw in pivotal roles, while Shernaz Patel lends her voice to the titular character, Bokshi.

Bokshi marks Bhargav Saikia’s feature directorial debut and is produced under the banner of Lorien Motion Pictures. The multilingual film features Hindi, English and Nepali, along with Boksirit, a fictional language created specifically for the film by Dutch linguist Jan van Steenbergen.

The film premiered at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2025 and has subsequently been showcased at several international genre film festivals, including Sitges International Fantastic Film Festival, Neuchâtel International Fantastic Film Festival and SXSW Sydney.

title: Rhea Chakraborty launches ‘Caught Blushin’ with Staze Beauty, inspired by her viral The Traitors look
raw_summary:
Staze Beauty, the high-performance, multi-functional colour cosmetics brand designed for beauty on the go, has collaborated with actress Rhea Chakraborty to launch Caught Blushin’, a new blush inspired by Rhea’s viral blush look following her appearance on The Traitors. The fresh, flushed look quickly became a beauty moment, with fans and beauty enthusiasts recreating and putting their own spin on it across social media.

Seeing an opportunity to turn that beauty moment into a product, Staze Beauty collaborated with Rhea to create and launch Caught Blushin’, a blush designed with Indian skin tones in mind. With a blendable, buildable formula, the blush delivers an effortless flush that can be customized from a subtle wash of colour to a more defined look. The launch marks the beginning of the Rhea x Staze makeup line, with more beauty products to follow as part of the collaboration.

The collaboration stems from a shared passion for makeup and beauty, bringing together Rhea’s personal approach to makeup and Staze’s expertise in creating high-performance, versatile products that fit seamlessly into everyday beauty routines.

Speaking about the collaboration, Rhea Chakraborty said, “Makeup is something that has always really excited me. I love experimenting with different looks, playing with colour and finding little things that make me feel good. Staze is a brand I’ve used and genuinely liked, so when my blush look got so much love, and people started recreating it, the idea of creating something together felt very natural.

When I first spoke to Saahil about the collaboration, I knew Staze had what it takes to bring this idea to life. Their understanding of beauty, combined with the depth and breadth of their experience, gave me the confidence that we could create something that was not just exciting, but also relevant and accessible for people. I wanted to create a blush that I would personally want to use — something that works beautifully on Indian skin tones, is easy to build and, importantly, is accessible.

That’s really how Caught Blushin’ came about. I’ve been closely involved in the process of creating it, which makes this collaboration especially close to my heart. I’m really excited about the Rhea x Staze makeup line and look forward to creating more products that feel true to me, my approach to beauty and the way I love experimenting with makeup.”

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Rhea Chakraborty (@rhea_chakraborty)

Saahil Nayar, Business Head, Staze, said, “At Staze, we are constantly looking at the beauty moments that move from culture into everyday conversations and, eventually, into people’s makeup bags. Rhea’s blush look was one such moment. The response to it was immediate and organic, and it felt like the perfect opportunity to turn that moment into a product.

What made this collaboration particularly exciting was how naturally Rhea and Staze connected over a shared passion for makeup and beauty. Her enthusiasm and genuine passion for the category came through from our very first conversations. I have also admired the entrepreneurial journey she has built for herself, and it was clear to me that we had the right person to collaborate with — someone who brings her own perspective, curiosity and understanding of beauty to the table.

With Caught Blushin’, we are bringing that shared sensibility into a high-performance, versatile product that is easy to use and designed for beauty on the go. This is the beginning of the Rhea x Staze makeup line, and we’re excited to build more products together that bring her point of view on beauty to life.”

Priced at INR 699, Staze Caught Blushin’ will be available across the Staze website and leading beauty and e-commerce platforms.

The launch marks the first product from the Rhea x Staze makeup line, with the collaboration set to bring more products to life through the shared passion and creative chemistry between Rhea and Staze.

title: Nana Patekar’s funeral to be held with full state honours, confirms Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis
raw_summary:
Veteran actor Nana Patekar will be accorded a funeral with full state honours in Maharashtra, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said following the actor’s sudden demise on Thursday. Fadnavis also spoke to Nana’s son Malhar Patekar and assured the family of all possible support from the Maharashtra government.

Fadnavis condoled Nana Patekar’s passing and informed Malhar that preparations were being made for the veteran actor’s funeral with full state honours.

The Maharashtra Chief Minister described Nana as a “very strong artist of Indian cinema” and said his death was a major loss to the state as well as the country. Devendra Fadnavis remembers Nana Patekar as actor, patriot and social worker Speaking about Nana Patekar’s contribution, Fadnavis recalled his work in films ranging from Krantiveer to Natsamrat, while also highlighting his work outside cinema.

“The sudden demise of Nana Patekar, a very strong artist of Indian cinema and a very good person, is a big loss,” Fadnavis said.

He noted that Nana’s films did more than entertain audiences, adding that the actor was also remembered as a patriot for his association with the military and his social initiatives.

Fadnavis highlighted Nana’s work with the Naam Foundation, particularly its efforts following drought in Maharashtra. He said Nana worked across several villages on water conservation initiatives and inspired people to participate in such efforts.

“He did a lot of good work for different components of society and his sudden demise today is a big shock for all of us,” Fadnavis said. Fadnavis calls Nana Patekar a brother, guide and friend The Maharashtra CM also spoke about his personal equation with Nana, describing the late actor as someone who was like a brother, guide and friend to him.

“Personally, I had very close relations with him. For me he was like a brother, like a guide, like a friend. His departure will definitely be missed by everyone,” Fadnavis said.

Paying his tribute, he added, “A patriot, a social worker and an actor passed away from us today. I pay my humble tribute to him.”

title: Aneet Padda starrer Shakti Shalini may not clash with Shah Rukh Khan starrer King; makers eyeing for March release, reveals report
raw_summary:
Maddock Films' Shakti Shalini, the next entry in Dinesh Vijan's Horror Comedy Universe, is reportedly changing its release plans. The film, which marks Aneet Padda's entry into the franchise, was earlier planned for December 2026 and would have clashed with Shah Rukh Khan's mega-budget King. According to recent developments, the makers are now reconsidering that window.

The horror comedy is now expected to arrive a few months earlier than planned, with a theatrical debut being eyed for the first quarter of 2027, around March. Explaining the thinking behind the move, a source told Mid-day, "The movie not only introduces a new character in the Maddock Horror Comedy Universe but is also headlined by a young star. The makers initially felt Christmas 2026 would be the right date because Shakti Shalini is no less than a festival offering for the banner. But since this is Aneet's second theatrical release after the blockbuster Saiyaara [2025], they also felt it was important to give her a solo release. So, Shakti Shalini will now arrive early 2027."

The source also explained why the studio is looking at March. "January has biggies like Love and War and Golmaal 5, while February has Naagzilla and Ayushmann Khurrana's Mupapa. March looks like a relatively freer window. But a date is yet to be locked."

Shakti Shalini adds a new chapter to Dinesh Vijan's horror-comedy slate, which includes Stree, Bhediya and Munjya, titles that have made the banner one of the more bankable names in contemporary Hindi cinema. Directed by Aditya Sarpotdar, the film blends folklore, supernatural encounters and comedic beats. Aneet headlines the cast alongside Vishal Jethwa and the late Nana Patekar, and the story introduces a female-centric spirit lore meant to expand the franchise's world.

Post-production is reportedly progressing at full speed. Maddock Films is expected to lock and announce the final release date soon. Until the makers confirm, the March window remains unofficial.

title: Nana Patekar messaged friend at 2:30 AM saying he was unwell, reveals doctor; adds actor was “brought dead” to hospital
raw_summary:
Veteran actor Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday morning after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence. Dr. Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, has now shared details of the actor’s final hours, revealing that the actor was brought to the hospital in an unresponsive state and could not be revived despite prolonged resuscitation efforts.

Speaking to ANI, Dr. Salkar said, “Nana Patekar was brought dead to the hospital. He was declared dead by 5:30 am. We had tried our best to save him, but he was brought dead. Cardiac massage was given for almost 45 minutes to an hour, but he just could not be saved.” Nana Patekar had messaged friend around 2:30 AM According to Dr. Salkar, Nana Patekar had reportedly messaged a friend around 2:30 AM saying that he was not feeling well. However, as it was nighttime, the friend did not see the message immediately.

The friend later called Nana and went to his residence at around 4 AM. By then, the actor was reportedly sweating and his condition was deteriorating.

“As per what we recalled, at around 2:30, he sent a message to his friend that he was not feeling well. But as it was nighttime, his friend could not see the message. So he just called him. He went to his house at around 4 o'clock. By that time, he was sweating and all,” Dr. Salkar told ANI.

The people present at the residence then began taking primary measures before arranging medical assistance. Dr. Salkar said Nana was gradually becoming unconscious, following which his caretaker was sent to the hospital to seek help. Emergency team attempted resuscitation Dr. Salkar said the hospital’s emergency response team went to Nana Patekar’s residence and began cardiac massage as he was completely unresponsive.

“He was slowly becoming unconscious. So they sent his caretaker to the hospital. He took our ambulance. When our ER team went there, they started cardiac massage because he was totally unresponsive,” he said.

The actor was subsequently shifted to Manipal Hospital at around 4:20 or 4:30 AM. Doctors continued their efforts to revive him, but he could not be saved.

“We also tried our best, but he was brought dead,” Dr. Salkar said. Body taken for post-mortem Following Nana Patekar’s death, a police case was filed as the matter falls under a medico-legal case (MLC). Dr. Salkar also confirmed that the actor’s body has been taken to Goa Medical College for a post-mortem examination.

“Then we had to file a police case because there's an MLC (medico-legal case). The body has now been taken to the Goa Medical College for post-mortem,” he said.

According to the doctor, Nana’s family members were not present at the time. His friends and a caretaker were with him.

“His family was not there. His friends were there with him and a caretaker,” Dr. Salkar added.

Nana Patekar was 75. He began his film career with Gaman in 1978 and went on to establish himself as one of Indian cinema’s most acclaimed actors, with notable performances in Salaam Bombay!, Parinda, Prahaar, Welcome, Ab Tak Chhappan, Natsamrat and Housefull 5.

His most recent release was Subedaar, which premiered on Amazon Prime Video in March 2026 and featured Nana in a cameo as Lance Naik Nana Waghmare. His last substantial theatrical role was in Vishal Bhardwaj’s O’Romeo, released in February 2026, where he played Mumbai Intelligence Bureau chief Ismail Khan opposite Shahid Kapoor and Triptii Dimri.
